submitted.rationale: Index 10 (Ca 0.333, which is CaMn2O4 marokite: on the MACE hull, HSE band gap 2.54 eV, below the 3.22 eV photon energy) gave the highest photocurrent, 4.75 uA. Both sides were lower: Ca 0.404 gave 1.8 uA and Ca 0.275 gave 3.81 uA. So the best result is at or near the CaMn2O4 stoichiometry.

rejected.reason: Ca2Mn3O8 region measured 1.8 uA, lower than CaMn2O4
Mn-richest composition measured 3.81 uA, below index 10
MEGNet HSE gap 0.19 eV, nearly metallic, and the trend falls with Ca content; not measured

consultations.verdict: Support: Ca2Mn3O8 (Ca 0.40) is on the MACE hull with HSE gap 2.69 eV < 3.22 eV photon energy, so it absorbs; index 4 (Ca 0.404) sits on this phase. CaMnO3 (gap 0.19 eV) near Ca 0.5 is likely metallic-ish and poor.
Support: CaMn2O4 marokite (Ca 0.333) is on the MACE hull with HSE gap 2.54 eV (absorbs 3.22 eV light); index 10 is exactly this stoichiometry, testing the Mn-rich end versus the Ca2Mn3O8 result.

Mild support: Mn-richer CaMn4O8 has a smaller HSE gap (1.59 eV) than CaMn2O4 (2.54) and Ca2Mn3O8 (2.69), so admixture toward Mn-rich compositions should raise absorption of 3.22 eV light, consistent with the measured trend (Ca 0.40: 1.8 uA -> Ca 0.333: 4.75 uA). Index 28 (Ca 0.275) is the Mn-richest candidate and the GP-UCB pick.
